newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Hungary outlines case for NATO membership.
newsitem.headline: Hungary outlines case for NATO membership.

text.p: Hungarian Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs outlined his country's case to be one of the first new NATO members for over two decades during talks at the alliance's headquarters in Brussels on Wednesday.
Kovacs met the ambassadors of the 16 current member states as part of a final round of talks between NATO and all the candidate countries from former communist Europe aspiring for full membership.
Hungary, along with Poland and the Czech Republic, is one of the favourites to win membership at the first attempt.

NATO countries are to hold a summit in Madrid in July at which certain countries will be invited to join. The formal negotiations would then be concluded by the end of the year, leaving two years for ratification by member states' parliaments.
"NATO decided to hold one more round of talks with the applicants to give them one last chance to press their case," said one official.
